WITH obese_kids AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT co.person_id
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.descendant_concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
  JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = co.person_id

    AND DATEDIFF(YEAR, DATEFROMPARTS(p.year_of_birth, ISNULL(p.month_of_birth,1), ISNULL(p.day_of_birth,1)), co.condition_start_date) < 18
),
mh AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT descendant_concept_id AS mh_concept_id
  FROM omop.concept_ancestor
  WHERE ancestor_concept_id = 432586
)
SELECT TOP 25 c.concept_name AS mental_health_dx,
       COUNT(DISTINCT co.person_id) AS n_children
FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
JOIN obese_kids ok ON ok.person_id = co.person_id
JOIN mh ON mh.mh_concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
JOIN omop.concept c ON c.concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
GROUP BY c.concept_name
ORDER BY n_children DESC
SELECT TOP 5 person_id, COUNT(*) n FROM omop.condition_occurrence GROUP BY person_id ORDER BY n DESC

## Children with obesity: most common co-occurring mental health diagnoses

Cohort: **39,428** children (<18 at time of obesity diagnosis) in the OMOP EHR database. Counts below are distinct children carrying each mental-health diagnosis.

| Diagnosis | Children | % of cohort |
|---|---|---|
| Anxiety disorder | 3,734 | 9.5% |
| Depressive disorder | 3,147 | 8.0% |
| ADHD (all types) | ~2,479+ | 6.3%+ |
| Autism spectrum disorder | 2,333 | 5.9% |
| Major depressive disorder | 1,456 | 3.7% |
| Generalized anxiety disorder | 1,046 | 2.7% |
| Acute stress disorder | 1,020 | 2.6% |
| Post-traumatic stress disorder | 829 | 2.1% |
| Anorexia nervosa / eating disorders | 622 / 602 | 1.6% |
| Adjustment disorder | 605 | 1.5% |

(ADHD is fragmented across subtype codes — combined 1,133 + inattentive 961 + parent code 2,479 — so it is effectively the 2nd–3rd most common if pooled.)

**Headline:** the dominant cluster is **anxiety + depression + ADHD + ASD**, followed by trauma/stress disorders (acute stress, PTSD, adjustment) and eating disorders.

## Plausible appetite/stress pathways linking them

> Note: the biomedical knowledge graph timed out on every query (including single indexed lookups), so these mechanistic links are drawn from established physiology rather than confirmed against the KG. Treat them as hypotheses to verify against primary sources.

- **HPA axis / cortisol (stress → depression, anxiety, PTSD).** Chronic stress raises CRH → ACTH → cortisol, which promotes visceral adiposity and hyperphagia for energy-dense food. This is the strongest shared link for the stress-disorder cluster (acute stress, PTSD, adjustment, GAD) with weight gain.
- **Leptin–melanocortin (POMC → MC4R) signaling.** Central regulator of satiety; leptin resistance in obesity co-tracks with depressive symptoms ("leptin resistance" hypothesis of depression). MC4R also modulates anxiety-like behavior.
- **Serotonin (5-HT) & dopamine reward.** 5-HT links satiety with mood (shared target of SSRIs); dopaminergic reward/reward-deficiency ties food-seeking to ADHD and to binge/eating disorders.
- **Ghrelin & NPY/AgRP (orexigenic).** Ghrelin rises with stress and stimulates appetite while also being anxiolytic/antidepressant acutely — a candidate node coupling stress, mood, and feeding.
- **Neuroinflammation (IL-6, TNF-α, CRP).** Adipose-derived inflammation is associated with both depression and impaired satiety signaling — a shared biological substrate.
- **BDNF.** Low BDNF is implicated in both energy balance/satiety and depression/anxiety; BDNF–TrkB is downstream of MC4R.
- **Iatrogenic loop.** Second-generation antipsychotics and some mood/ADHD-adjacent medications drive weight gain (H1/5-HT2C antagonism), a non-biological but clinically major link.
